title: Working hard over here … continued.
author: denver_erik
selftext:
First of all thanks to all that made comments on my previous post. I did a terrible job of explaining where this is at. We’ve tested this for months. Probably six months at this point and we have several bots. We’re using live money. This is my personal account. We have several of these running I think at this point as many as we could get into broker houses. 

So technically we probably have about 10 of them running between the two of us. They don’t all perform the same. Some are about a third of this. Plenty of history.  I don’t believe you need five years of history. Would that be nice yes, but I’m not gonna step over four grand a month for for one bot and paper trade for five years, five years of history. I think we’ve got it. And I appreciate everyone’s advice. Is there a risk yes. Of course there’s a risk. i think we understand that. We have saved guards and there’s only a limited amount of stocks on the table at a time 

As you can tell by the chart, volatility matters. Towards the end, those low bars, I’m at a franchise event this week and had to travel. I couldn’t sit around and babysit this. It had lower numbers. Because I wasn’t trading enough, about two days I wasn’t trading at all this week. 

There’s no smoke and  mirrors here. I own businesses, I’m a real person. I really do this.  I don’t need any of your money and I’m not asking for it. If you have some advice, I’ll take it and make this better. I really don’t give a shit if people believe this or not. I’m making money on it. 

If you wanna collaborate on anything, let me know or if you want to be skeptical good luck on your ventures.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: with ten bots between the two of you, check how many share the same entry logic. if most do, a bad week hits all ten on the same day, and your real exposure is the sum of them, not any one bot's limit.

replies.author: denver_erik
replies.body: They all share the same logic

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: then it's really one bot sized ten times. I'd add the ten positions up and look at the worst day the group would have had together, that's the number you're actually carrying.

replies.author: denver_erik
replies.body: Thank you I know how to run mathematical models. They are all positive. I think the lowest one does about 30 to 75 per day. However, keep in mind the variables for production are great and we still don’t know all the answers. Some of it has to do with Internet connection, some of it has to do with bandwidth, the particular stock, computer, the volatility of the sector that the stock is in, there are so many different variables. However, they’re all positive.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
those production variables are the whole gap, dropped connections and real fills never show up in a model. I'd let all ten run on paper against live quotes for a few weeks before adding size. hosting that kind of trial run is the whole job of Quantradin, which I built, though only for US stocks and options, not crypto.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Sharing live results from your own account is more than most people do. One number I'd look at is the total before fees, since with this many trades the fees can take a big share of a small profit per trade, and the after-fee figure is the one that matters. It also helps to compare the win rate with the break-even win rate, because a high win rate with small gains can still lose on a few bad days. The point that results depend on volatility is useful, so I'd track how it does in quiet weeks too. Cymetica's Backtest Labs has a fee setting and a held out stretch of data for checks like that.

comments.author: denver_erik
comments.body:
I just wanted to provide an update. Today George (the bot) did very poorly. This whole week it has done poorly. There was at least two days in the last week or so that I had not traded at all. Today the same bot did only $23 of profit. After fees.

As I had stated previously, I am at a convention this week. I am using a free guest WiFi since I’m at this convention.  With these fast penny scalp trades, you are literally looking at milliseconds to seconds. The Achilles heel is obviously your connection and your latency. All the more reason to do a virtual server. The optimization I am looking at next is connection optimization, stock optimization, as well as where the bot lives. One thing I know is that 50% of all the profit on here comes from one stock. The four others are the remaining.

I understand the security matters of a public connection and they’re taken care of.
